answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents post stake to cross-audit peer transaction graphs. When audits detect suspicious clusters, topological cut verifications measure edge connectivity across clusters; sparse cuts isolate coordinated fake nodes, instantly slashing their stake. This forces attacker cost to scale superlinearly with cluster size: creating a hollow ring of puppets in an isolated tundra provides zero leverage, while reaching the zenith of network influence demands unrecoverable capital.
